correctness.rationale: For L=lcm(2,4,...,20)=5040 and P10 the first ten positive Euler factors, exact polynomial identity P10(q)S5(q)=H(q)/(1-q^5040)^10 follows from finite geometric sums. Independently multiplied the ten odd factors and ten bounded even geometric factors, using a separate exact integer recurrence, and checked every one of 50412 coefficients of H: none negative, zeros exactly {0,1,2,26,30}. Since every H_{r+5040}>0 for residues 0<=r<5040, all P10S5 coefficients n>=5040 are strictly positive. For n<5040, only 26 and 30 remain; the omitted positive Euler tail contributes a q^21 term and P10S5 coefficients 5=1 and 9=3, proving b(26),b(30)>0. This is an all-index algebraic proof with a fully exhausted finite polynomial certificate, not finite sampling of P(q)S5(q).
